population.span: We conducted a randomized, double-blind, double-dummy trial comparing two once-daily regimens of edoxaban with warfarin in 21,105 patients with moderate-to-high-risk atrial fibrillation (median follow-up, 2.8 years).

endpoint.span: The primary efficacy end point was stroke or systemic embolism.

estimate.span: In the intention-to-treat analysis, there was a trend favoring high-dose edoxaban versus warfarin (hazard ratio, 0.87; 97.5% CI, 0.73 to 1.04; P=0.08)

ci.span: In the intention-to-treat analysis, there was a trend favoring high-dose edoxaban versus warfarin (hazard ratio, 0.87; 97.5% CI, 0.73 to 1.04; P=0.08)

analysis_set.span: In the intention-to-treat analysis, there was a trend favoring high-dose edoxaban versus warfarin

treatment_strategy.span:
ARM: Warfarin/placebo edoxaban [ACTIVE_COMPARATOR] Warfarin tablets plus placebo Edoxaban tablets
ARM: high dose edoxaban/placebo warfarin [EXPERIMENTAL] Edoxaban tablets (60mg) plus warfarin placebo tablets

follow_up.span: 21,105 patients with moderate-to-high-risk atrial fibrillation (median follow-up, 2.8 years).

entry_population_reading.span: Exclusion Criteria: * Transient atrial fibrillation secondary to other reversible disorders * Subjects with moderate or severe mitral stenosis, unresected atrial myxoma, or a mechanical heart valve

entry_population.extractor_why: The registry specifies adults aged at least 21 with documented AF and excludes moderate or severe mitral stenosis and mechanical heart valves; the estimate is explicitly intention-to-treat.

extractor_mismatch_note: The served HR 0.87 matches the high-dose intention-to-treat estimate, but the served CI 0.745–1.016 is not printed in any held source. The served provenance describes a conversion to 95%; the abstract reports 97.5% CI 0.73–1.04. Bind the reported interval and retain any conversion as a separate derived calculation.

derivation.check: the printed limits are near-symmetric on the log scale about 0.87 (geometric midpoint 0.8713), so the rescaling is faithful; CORRECTION after second adjudication: the printed 97.5% limits are rounded to 2 dp, so the derived 95% limits are APPROXIMATE (rounding error of the order of +/-0.003), not exact. The registry also prints a 99% CI .709 to 1.068 for the ITT superiority analysis.
